newsitem.title: FRANCE: Britain could face legal action in mad cow crisis.
newsitem.headline: Britain could face legal action in mad cow crisis.

text.p: A major actor in a European Parliament probe of mad cow disease said on Tuesday Britain should face legal action for failing to cooperate in its work.

Committee Chairman Reimer Boege told Reuters Britain had refused to send Agriculture Minister Douglas Hogg to testify before the committee of inquiry, violating an accord between the parliament and national governments.
"This is explosive stuff," he said, saying action had not been taken so far as the committee had not wanted to push Britain into a more uncooperative stance.

The committee will decide whether to follow this line of action on February 6 when it finalises a critical report on Britain and the Commission's handling of the crisis surrounding BSE (bovine spongiform encephalopathy).
In London Hogg -- who refused to give evidence to the committee in person when he was invited late last year -- shrugged off the calls.
"If they bring legal action of that kind they will lose it," Hogg told BBC radio in an interview.
The full European Parliament is set to vote on the report on February 19.
Boege, a German Christian Democrat, said a principle was at stake. "It is not just a case of Hogg but the future of all committees of inquiry," he said.
But he acknowledged the Commission was unlikely to consider legal action while a British general election, which must be called by May 22, is on the horizon.
